content.headline: Eurozone expands to 21 states as Bulgaria joins
content.body: The euro area now comprises 21 member states, following the adoption of the single currency by Bulgaria on January 1. The European Commission confirmed the move, marking a significant step in the bloc's economic integration. Bulgaria becomes the first new eurozone member since Croatia joined in 2023. The country had met all convergence criteria, including price stability and sound public finances. With the addition, the eurozone's population rises to over 350 million. The European Central Bank will oversee monetary policy for the new member, and Bulgarian banks have been integrated into the Eurosystem. This expansion strengthens the euro's global role, though some economists warn of challenges ahead. The change is effective immediately, with the lev being replaced by the euro at a fixed rate. The eurozone now accounts for about 14% of global GDP.
